caption: A 3x2 loop: observer O1 (1,0) watches O5 (2,0) and powers lamp L (0,0) behind it; O2 (0,1) watches L, O3 (1,1) watches O2, O4 (2,1) watches O3, O5 (2,0) watches O4. The lamp goes dark 4 gt after its power ends, so O2 sees two edges per pass.
Two observers face to face: each watches the other, so every output change of one is a shape update in front of the other. Kicked by placing the second observer (B) last.
Four observers in a horizontal square, each watching the previous one (A <- D <- C <- B <- A): one 2 gt pulse travels around, 2 gt per observer. Kicked by placing B last.
Six observers around a 3x2 rectangle, each watching the previous one. Kicked by placing B last.

Torch + delay-1 repeater loop (draft, clk-rt): T (wall torch on A) -> 3 dust -> repeater R -> A. Inner loop period 4 * (1 + 1) = 8 gt: 7 x 8 = 56 <= 60, so the torch burns out at its 8th turn-off; R keeps T's input powered past that turn-off, so the 160 gt burnout re-check is not replaced by a relight tick, and T relights 160 gt after its 8th turn-off. Predicted period 220.

BURNOUT clock, 9 blocks (clk-rt): the 9-block torch + repeater loop with a delay-1 repeater. Inner loop period 8 (7 x 8 = 56 <= 60): the torch burns out at its 8th turn-off and relights 160 gt later (the repeater still powers it at that turn-off): period 4 + 56 + 160 = 220.

Comparator subtract clock, 8 blocks (draft, clk-rt): rear = redstone block (15); the output strongly powers block A; dust beside A carries A's strength to the comparator's side. Expected: output 15 / 1 alternating every 2 gt (period 4); the side dust 14 / 0.
Comparator subtract clock (draft, clk-rt): rear = redstone block (15), output -> 3 dust -> side. Expected: output alternates 15 / 2 every 2 gt (period 4), the last dust 13 / 0.

Torch + repeater loop, 9 blocks (draft, clk-rt): wall torch T on A -> repeater R reads T directly -> R strongly powers F -> dust beside F -> dust pointing into A. One inversion, loop delay 2 + 2d: period 4 (1 + d) = 12 with the delay-2 repeater (16 / 20 with delay 3 / 4).
C -> repeater(4) -> dust -> dust -> repeater(1) -> piston behind C: retraction at A+20, dist 1.

Self-starting: R is placed powered with no input; its turn-off is the first observer pulse. Calibrated sensor C strongly powers the stone below it; repeater R (delay 4) reads that stone; observer O (above R) watches R and plays note block N (diagonal to C: dist sqrt2, travel 1).
C -> repeater (4) -> stone X -> wall torch T on X's north face -> note block N diagonal to C.
Self-starting: R is placed powered with no input; its turn-off is the first observer pulse. Calibrated sensor C -> repeater R (delay 4) -> observer O watching R -> note block N (dist sqrt5).
Self-starting: calibrated C -> repeater R (delay 4, placed powered) -> observer O watching R -> note block N in line (dist 3 from C): event at A+20, travel 3.
Self-starting: fence gate E placed open+powered with no power closes on its placement update (BLOCK_CLOSE); then observer O's 3rd pulse on C opens it each period.
Self-starting: iron trapdoor placed open+powered with no power closes on its placement update.
Self-starting: piston placed extended (with its head) and unpowered retracts on its placement update (BLOCK_DEACTIVATE); then O's 3rd pulse on C moves it each period.

Self-starting 3-block clock: calibrated C, observer O watching C, oak trapdoor E behind O placed open+powered with no power: it closes on its placement update (BLOCK_CLOSE wakes C); then O's pulses at A+2, A+12, A+22 open/close E and only the A+22 one is heard (C re-arms at A+20).
Calibrated sensor C watched by observer O, note block N behind O (dist 2 from C).
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, piston E behind O (dist 2): O's 3rd pulse (A+22) extends E.
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, sticky piston E behind O (dist 2), facing away.
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, stone strongly powered by O, note block beyond it (dist 3).
C, observer O watching C, observer Q watching O (sideways), note block N behind Q (dist sqrt5): Q's 3rd pulse at A+24.
C, two observers in line, note block N (dist 3): 3rd pulse at A+24, travel 3.
C, three observers curling back (O watches C, Q watches O, R watches Q), note block N diagonal to C: A+26, travel 1.
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, EMPTY dispenser behind O: it fires 4 gt after each rising edge (empty dispense = BLOCK_ACTIVATE); the A+22 pulse fires it at A+26, heard at dist 2.
Plain sensor C (30 active + 10 cooldown), observer O watching C, note block behind O (dist 2): O's pulse after C's COOLDOWN->INACTIVE (A+42) plays the note.
Plain sensor C, observer O watching C, empty dispenser behind O (fires 4 gt after O's A+42 pulse).

Pure vibration ring (nothing but sensors changes state): calibrated sensors S1 (1,0,0), S2 (15,0,8), S3 (1,0,16), each with an amethyst block beside it; when S_i activates its amethyst resonates and S_(i+1) hears it floor(dist) = 15 gt later. P = 3 x 15. A1 is out of S3's range (dist^2 257), so after the kick only S2 wakes; afterwards the sensor two hops ahead is always still in its 20 gt dead time. Kick: right-click the note block K (only S1 is within 16 of it; S1 faces east so its back, K, gets no power from it).

Hopper slosh, 4 blocks (clk-item): two hoppers facing each other hold one item; it hops back and forth, 7 gt per hop (the receiving hopper was empty: TransferCooldown 8 - 1). A comparator reading the west hopper is on 7 gt, off 7 gt. redsim: P=14 gt, warmup 3, family comparator+hopper, 4 blocks, output on 7/14 gt, 1 rising edge(s)

Ring lock, 10 blocks (clk-item): 8 hoppers around a 3x3 square with a comparator in the middle that reads the west hopper and points into the east one, locking it whenever the west one holds an item; 4 swords. The lock makes the items queue and overtake: period 15 gt. redsim: P=15 gt, warmup 122, family comparator+hopper, 10 blocks, output on 7/15 gt, 1 rising edge(s)

Ring lock, 10 blocks (clk-item): 8 hoppers around a 3x3 square, a comparator in the middle reads the west hopper and locks the east one (it points into it); 3 items (2 stone + 1 sword). Items queue at the locked hopper and are released in an irregular order: the whole pattern repeats only every 654 gt. redsim: P=654 gt, warmup 22, family comparator+hopper, 10 blocks, output on 234/654 gt, 30 rising edge(s)

Dropper ring, 10 blocks (clk-item): hoppers and droppers around a 3x3 square, each passing items to the next; a comparator in the middle reads one ring container and points into the opposite one, a dropper: each time an item arrives under the comparator, the dropper fires 4 gt later (rising edge) and pushes one item on. Items wait in the droppers for a trigger, so the cycle is not a multiple of 7: 20 gt. redsim: P=20 gt, warmup 34, family comparator+dropper+hopper, 10 blocks, output on 7/20 gt, 1 rising edge(s)

A 3x2 loop of five observers and a note block: observer O1 (1,0,0) watches O5 (2,0,0) and powers the note block N (0,0,0) behind it; O2 (0,0,1) watches N, O3 (1,0,1) watches O2, O4 (2,0,1) watches O3, O5 watches O4. Jukebox carousel, 9 blocks (clk-item): 3 copies of disc 11 go around a jukebox J. A playing jukebox emits 15: it locks the extractor hopper below it, powers the inserter dropper beside it, keeps the torch standing on it off, and lights a 2-dust line whose second dust sits on a note block next to the lift dropper. When the song ends (lengthInTicks + 20 gt) the extractor pushes its waiting disc into the lift and pulls the played one; the torch relights 2 gt later and fires the inserter through the cell above it (4 gt): the next disc goes in. The new song lights the dust, the note block flips and fires the lift 4 gt later: the waiting disc rises into the inserter. Period = song + 6 gt, whatever the hopper tick order.

Census find (3x1x2, k<=5): a calibrated sensor and a plain sensor side by side, two observers (one watching the calibrated sensor, one watching that observer) and a note block: the calibrated sensor's own observer loop runs every 26 gt and the plain sensor, hearing the same note at most once per 40 gt, repeats every 130 gt = 5 loops (output: the plain sensor).

Census find (3x1x2, k<=5): two sensors and two empty dispensers: an observer on the calibrated sensor fires one dispenser, the other sits by the plain sensor; each sensor hears the dispensers at most once per dead time and gates the dispenser it powers; the joint cycle repeats every 135 gt (output: a full-period sensor).

Census find (4x1x2, k<=4): two sensors and one dispenser. A calibrated sensor watched by an observer that fires an empty dispenser runs its own 28 gt loop (the c28 clock); the plain sensor behind it hears the same dispenser at most once per 40 gt dead time (its power into the calibrated sensor's back is a frequency filter at 10, the dispenser's own frequency, so the loop keeps running): the plain sensor's cycle repeats every 140 gt = 5 loops (output: the plain sensor).

Census find (3x1x2, k<=5): two sensors, an observer on the calibrated one, an empty dispenser and a note block: the calibrated sensor's observer loop and the plain sensor's 40 gt dead time interlock (each powers and gates a neighbor), repeating every 212 gt (output: a full-period sensor).

Census find (3x1x2, k<=5): two sensors, an observer on the calibrated one, a note block and an empty dispenser: the calibrated sensor's observer loop and the plain sensor's 40 gt dead time interlock (each powers and gates a neighbor), repeating every 215 gt (output: a full-period sensor).

Census find (3x1x2, k<=5): a calibrated sensor with the plain sensor beside it, an observer, an empty dispenser and a note block: the calibrated sensor's loop runs every 24 gt and the plain sensor hears it at most once per 40 gt; their joint cycle repeats every 216 gt = 9 loops (output: the plain sensor).

Census find (3x3x1, k<=4): a piston, an observer on top watching it, an empty dispenser on top of the observer, and a calibrated sensor beside the observer whose power reaches the piston by quasi-connectivity (through the observer's cell); the piston's moves pulse the observer, the dispenser fires 4 gt later and the sensor hears it.

Census find (3x1x2, k<=5): three sensors (two calibrated, one plain) around an observer and an empty dispenser: each hears the dispenser at most once per dead time and gates what it powers; the joint cycle repeats every 242 gt (output: a full-period sensor).

Census find (4x1x2, k<=4): a sculk divider. Two observers facing each other (a 6 gt observer clock) pulse an empty dispenser beside a plain sensor; while the sensor is active it powers the dispenser, so only the first pulse after its re-arm fires it: the sensor fires every 7th cycle (output: the sensor).

Census find (4x1x2, k<=4): two sensors and one dispenser. An observer watching a plain sensor fires an empty dispenser beside a calibrated sensor; both sensors hear it, and the calibrated sensor, while active, powers the dispenser so pulses that come then are lost: the two dead times (20 and 40 gt) interlock into a 43 gt cycle.

Census find (3x1x2, k<=5): a sculk divider. An observer pair (6 gt) pulses an empty dispenser, which conducts the pulse into an oak trapdoor; the calibrated sensor hears them at most once per 20 gt dead time, and its own cycle repeats every 66 gt (output: the sensor).

Census find (3x1x2, k<=5): a calibrated sensor, a plain sensor and a second calibrated sensor around an observer and an empty dispenser: each hears the dispenser at most once per dead time and the sensors that power the dispenser block its triggers; the joint cycle repeats every 84 gt (output: a full-period sensor).

Census find (4x1x2, k<=4): a sculk divider. Two observers facing each other (a 6 gt observer clock) flip an oak trapdoor on every pulse; the plain sensor 3 blocks away hears it at most once per 40 gt dead time, and its own cycle repeats every 90 gt (output: the sensor).

Powder snow dispenser clock, 5 blocks (clk-item): a dispenser facing down holds one powder snow bucket; each fire toggles the cell under it (the bucket places powder snow and becomes an empty bucket; the empty bucket picks the powder snow back up). An observer watching that cell pulses (2 gt) into a dust behind it, which climbs onto the observer and powers the dispenser: each toggle re-fires the dispenser 2 + 4 gt later, P = 12. Kicked once (a stone flashed in the cell for 1 gt). JVM only (redsim does not model dispenser item behaviors).

Powder snow dispenser clock with a repeater, 5 blocks (clk-item): a dispenser facing down holds one powder snow bucket; each fire toggles the cell under it (place / pick up powder snow). An observer watching that cell pulses into a stone; the dust on the stone feeds a repeater standing on the observer that points into the dispenser. Each toggle re-fires the dispenser 2 (observer) + 2 x delay (repeater) + 4 (dispenser) gt later: P = 2 x (6 + 2 x delay) = 16, 20, 24, 28 for delay 1..4 (delay 1 here). Kicked once (a stone flashed in the cell for 1 gt). JVM only.

NESTED comparator COUNTER clock (clk-rt): an inner comparator fading ring (2 + 2 comparators) and 2 lossless counter rings (sizes 2-2, innermost first), each decremented by one level per refill pulse of the level inside it (the pulse cut to strength 1 by a subtract comparator with side 14) and refilled by its own torch at 0: period = about 14^2 inner periods

Rectangle ring (clk-rt): the 3x3 perimeter clockwise from the north-west corner = [b, c, b, c, b, c, b, c] (number = repeater delay, * = powered at placement, b = block, d = dust, T = wall torch on the block before it, c = comparator); 0 torches: a pulse ring of loop delay 8 gt; kicked by a redstone_wall_torch[facing=north,lit=true] at [0, 0, 0] for 2 gt at tick 0
